summary:
Core engine logic is correct and I could not break it: incremental refresh_customer is bit-identical to a full run_population, guardrails hold after customer confirmation, the fatigue cap caps the right set, and seed 42 is deterministic. The findings are in the operational and privacy edges around the engine, not the decision SQL. The two that matter most for a live demo and an audit are (1) any heavy or odd custom moment freezes the whole app because run_population holds the single DB lock for its entire duration, and (2) the README claim "counts under 10 are hidden" is contradicted by the product's own output.

Method and caveat: the live backend/data/mirror.duckdb (and .wal) is exclusively locked by the running server (python PIDs 35448 and 54084), so it could not be copied, even with shared-read open. I did not stop the server. Instead I regenerated seed 42 at 100,000 customers into the scratchpad. The result has the same file size as the live file (32,256,000 bytes), 6,116,388 events (README: 6.1M) and 5,436 planted truths. Two independent generations gave identical order-independent row-hash sums for customers, events and truth, so the seed-42 determinism claim holds. The live DB's runtime state (feedback, custom moments, cache) was therefore not inspected. All experiment scripts are in C:/Users/Dario/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Dario-OneDrive---Erasmushogeschool-Brussel-Hackathon-Tectronic-30-09-2026/3b438afa-ea49-4084-a20d-604844ed0009/scratchpad/corr/ (exp1.py to exp12.py, common.py). No project file was modified: nothing under the project root is newer than my first scratch file, and .env was never read. Timings were taken on a 16-logical-CPU machine that other processes were using at about 14 to 22%, so absolute numbers are noisy.

Checked and found correct (no issue):
- README results table reproduced exactly on the regenerated DB. buying_home 94.3% ask / 100% act / 63.0% recall; freelance 86.5 / 100 / 50.4; growing_family 45.6 / 100 / 50.3; moving_in 82.8 / 100 / 15.0; EV 99.8 / 100 / 26.5. The message share is 2.47%, rising to 2.91% with EV.
- Demo customers behave as the script says: Sofie buying_home 0.82 (ask) and growing_family 0.545 (ask); Lucas freelance 0.839 (act); Marc buying_home 0.874 (advisor). Advisor An's list has 46 customers (limit 50; Marc rank 1, Sofie rank 6). Advisor Jan's has 55 (Lucas rank 19). Checked before the EV moment is added.
- Incremental vs full consistency: 0 twin mismatches and 0 signal_hits mismatches, comparing exact floats, state, feedback and evidence. Scenarios: full vs full (100,000 customers), 642 refreshed customers with no change, about 290 customers with random confirm/reject feedback (including confirm-with-zero-evidence and three confirmations on one customer), and 300 consent changes. A second full run then matched the incremental results for ALL customers.
- Guardrails vs confirmed feedback: confirmed gives confidence 1.0, but min_age, vulnerable=advisor and vulnerable=suppress still win (blocked_guardrail, advisor). A feedback-only customer (no consent_app, no hits) can confirm buying_home and gets 'act' at 1.0, which is self-declaration by design; guardrails still apply to it.
- FULL OUTER JOIN of beliefs and feedback handles the feedback-without-signals case (inferred 0.0, evidence empty). rejected gives 0.0 and suppressed_feedback and wins over everything.
- row_number partition: PARTITION BY customer_id, (state0 IN ('act','ask')) puts only act/ask in the capped partition. advisor/wait/blocked/suppressed rows fall into the other partition and are never capped (see low finding). Ties are deterministic (confirmed first, then priority*confidence, then moment_id).
- Noisy-OR edge cases: ln(0) is unreachable through the DSL (weight is gt 0 and le 0.95, so the smallest term is ln 0.05); DuckDB does raise 'cannot take logarithm of zero' if a weight of 1.0 were inserted directly. Twelve signals at 0.95 give 0.9999999999999998, so evidence alone never reaches 1.0; an act threshold of 1.0 is reachable only by confirmation. Weight 0.9500001, 1.0 and 0 are all rejected.
- Locking: DB.execute/rows/scalar each take the RLock internally (db.py:31-47). my_preferences (api.py:264) is a single statement and is therefore serialized, so it is not a bug. Grep found no raw .con use outside db.py and generate.py. The Dockerfile runs a single uvicorn process. The real concurrency issues are F1, F3 and F11.
- Confounders: gift buyers really do produce the growing_family false positives (precision 46%). Not a bug, but noted: baby_store and baby_store_repeat are nested signals on the same events, so noisy-OR double counts them (3 baby purchases give 0.61, not 0.4). This looks deliberate, but it is not independent evidence.
- generate.py ignores the meta.sim_now it writes (engine uses config.SIM_NOW), so a different MIRROR_SIM_NOW at run time would silently shift every window (not executed).
- Generator determinism across numpy versions is not guaranteed by numpy (not tested).

findings.title: One heavy or odd custom moment freezes the entire app (global lock held for the whole run; cost unbounded)
findings.detail: run_population holds the single db.lock across both CTAS statements and stats() (engine.py:96-104). Every authenticated request calls state.db.one inside current_user (api.py:118), so all users block, including login. MAX_CUSTOM_MOMENTS=20 (config.py:43) bounds the number of moments, not the work: cost scales with signal_hits volume and the twin stage grows superlinearly. The 'run' rate limit (security.py, 6 per 60 s) does not help. The UI (ProductOwner.tsx:41-58) chains add then run with no timeout or cancel. A judge editing the live EV JSON to a common kind (e.g. login, groceries) triggers a long freeze.
findings.evidence: exp5.py and exp7.py on the 100k scratch DB. Baseline 4 built-ins: run_ms 2762/3188/3041. After adding 16 'wide' custom moments (20 moments, 206 signals, common tx kinds, within_days 365): run_ms=726,649 (12 minutes), signal_hits=15,122,247, beliefs=1,495,926, and a trivial db.rows('SELECT 1') issued 0.5 s into the run waited 726.9 s for the lock. One 12-signal moment: hits 2.0 s + twin 11.0 s, 1,036,207 hits. One app 'login' signal (weight 0.5, ask 0.3): twin 8.9 s and 86.6% of all customers get a message (86,636). Forced-single-moment timings are noisy because the machine was shared, but the unbounded, lock-held behaviour does not depend on that.
findings.fix: (1) Compute into staging tables (twin_new, signal_hits_new) outside the global lock, then swap with a short transaction; or use a per-request con.cursor() and let DuckDB MVCC serve readers during the write. (2) Add a cost guard before go-live: dry-run the new moment on a customer sample or COUNT its hits and refuse if reach exceeds something like 10% or hits exceed a cap. (3) Add a statement timeout: threading.Timer(n, con.interrupt). (4) For the demo, rehearse only the provided EV JSON and tell the presenter not to let judges change kind or within_days to high-volume kinds.
findings.demo_impact: If a judge tweaks the live moment (plausible in a 'try it yourself' moment), the whole app hangs for 10 s to minutes with no feedback. The pre-built EV moment itself is fine (about 4 to 6 s here).

reasons:
The mechanism is real and I reproduced it, but the stated "high" severity and some wording are overstated for the demo.

**Confirmed in code**
- `DB.lock` is one process-wide RLock (db.py:29). Every `execute`, `rows` and `scalar` takes it (db.py:31-48).
- `run_population` holds it across `sync_runtime`, both CTAS statements and `stats()` (engine.py:96-104).
- Every authenticated route runs `state.db.one(...)` inside `current_user` (api.py:118). Login does the same (api.py:158). So all users block while a run is in progress.
- Nothing bounds the cost. `MAX_CUSTOM_MOMENTS=20` (config.py:43) caps the count only. The DSL limits a moment to 12 signals, `within_days` ≤ 365 and `kind` matching ID_PATTERN (dsl.py:38-45, 120). It never checks that the kind is rare.
- The "run" rate limit is 6 per 60 s (security.py:101) and does not limit duration. No `interrupt` or timeout exists anywhere in the backend (grep), and `api()` has no abort signal (api.ts:30-36).

**Reproduced**
- Method: I ran the exact `compile_hits` and `twin_sql` CTAS under `DB.lock` on a 100k-customer, 6.1M-event scratch copy, in `scratchpad/refute_heavy`. It is the same DuckDB size as the live DB. I did not import `mirror.config` (it loads `.env`), so `moments_rt` is rebuilt in the harness.
- A second thread issued `db.one("SELECT 1")` 0.5 s into each run. The wait on the lock matched the run time:

| Case | Run time | Lock wait |
|---|---|---|
| 4 built-ins + shipped EV moment | 1.7-2.8 s | 1.2-2.3 s |
| EV with `within_days=365`, `min_count=1`, no `min_amount` (same kinds) | 2.9 s | 2.4 s |
| EV with one signal swapped to app `login` | 6.4 s | 5.9 s |
| EV with all signals swapped to groceries, restaurants, login | 9.8 s | 9.4 s |
| 1 custom moment, 12 common-kind signals | 10.4 s | 10.0 s |
| 2 such moments | 21 s | 20.6 s |
| 4 such moments | 46 s | 45.7 s |

- The 4-moment case has 4.1M signal hits, and the twin stage grows superlinearly (5.7 s, 15.9 s, 40 s). I did not re-run the reviewer's 12-minute case with 16 moments.

**What the finding overstates**
- **The shipped demo moment is fine.** It takes about 2-3 s here, and README step 5 uses exactly that JSON. Tweaking thresholds, weights, `within_days`, `min_count` or `min_amount` on the existing kinds stays cheap (2.9 s).
- **A freeze needs a high-volume `kind`.** The judge would have to swap in kinds such as `login` or `groceries`. The web UI never shows kind names: `/api/po/signal-kinds` exists at api.py:441, but nothing under `web/src` calls it. Multi-minute freezes need many 12-signal moments, which means deliberate abuse of the product-owner account, not one live edit.
- **The UI does give feedback.** The Validate button is disabled, the message reads "Running it on every customer…", and the Run button shows "Running…" (ProductOwner.tsx:52, 91-92, 212). The page is not silently dead, and the app recovers when the run finishes. There is no polling, so a demo freeze only hurts someone clicking in another tab during the run.
- **"Unbounded" is loose.** It is bounded at 20 moments × 12 signals × 365 days, but that bound is minutes.

**Fix**
- The fix direction is sound (staging tables or a cursor, a cost guard, a statement timeout).
- For today, the practical mitigation is to rehearse only the shipped EV JSON.
- If a heavy custom moment is added, press Delete to remove it. The delete is queued behind the running statement and then re-runs the population.

The mechanism reproduces, but "high" and "a judge tweaking the EV JSON triggers a long freeze" overstate the demo risk. Medium fits.

I ran everything on a scratch copy of a fresh 100k-customer, 6.1M-event DB (scratchpad lockrepro_c3), with no project file edited and .env never read. Timings come from a shared 16-core machine, so expect noise.

What holds up
- engine.py:96-104: run_population holds db.lock across both CTAS statements and stats().
- db.py:29 uses a single RLock-guarded connection. api.py:118 (current_user) and api.py:158 (login) both call state.db.one, so every authenticated request and every login queues behind a run.
- Cost is not capped by any timeout or reach check. MAX_CUSTOM_MOMENTS=20 (config.py:43) and at most 12 signals per moment (dsl.py:120) only bound the count.
- The "run" rate limit (security.py:102) limits how often you can run, not how long a run takes.
- The UI chains add then run (ProductOwner.tsx:41-58). api.ts uses a bare fetch with no timeout or abort.

Measured scaling (run_ms, in-process; a parallel db.rows('SELECT 1') issued 0.5 s in waited for essentially the whole run)
| Case | Run time | Probe wait |
|---|---|---|
| 4 built-ins | 1.4-2.4 s | 1.05-2.05 s |
| Shipped EV example | 2.0 s | 1.6 s |
| One app 'login' signal, weight 0.5, ask 0.3 | 3.5 s | 3.15 s |
| Shipped EV JSON with its 3 kinds swapped to groceries/restaurants/login | 6.4 s | 6.1 s |
| 1 moment, 12 common signals | 12.0 s | 11.7 s |
| 2 such moments | 20.4 s | 20.1 s |
| 4 such moments | 44.8 s | 44.7 s |
| 8 such moments | 178 s | 178.5 s |

Cost is superlinear in the number of heavy moments, which matches the reviewer's 12 minutes at 20 moments.

HTTP level (TestClient, POST /api/po/run against a 12-signal moment, about 11 s)
- GET /api/me as a customer took 9.99 s.
- POST /api/auth/login took 10.07 s.
- GET /api/health, which never touches the db, took 0.27 s.

Why the severity and demo impact are overstated
- The shipped EV moment ran in about 2.0 s here, not the 4-6 s claimed. It is fine.
- The realistic "judge edits the JSON" cases cost 3.5-6.4 s here. A 10 s to minutes freeze needs a deliberately wide moment (12 common signals) or many of them.
- Only the product_owner role can add moments or trigger runs, so this is operator error, not an outside attack.
- A live 3-minute demo has one presenter. The PO button shows "Running…" and is disabled. The all-users lock only matters if someone else is using the app at the same moment.
- Even a normal run blocks everyone for its full 1.4-2.4 s, so blocking during a run is existing behaviour, not new.
- Recovery works: once the run ends, Remove plus re-run returns to about 2 s. The heavy moment stays saved until removed, so every later "Run on all customers" stays slow until then.

Fix viability
Separate DuckDB cursors let readers proceed during a write. In my test, SELECT count(*) FROM users took 3 ms and a twin lookup took 32 ms while a 4.2 s CTAS ran on another cursor. Fix (1) is therefore workable, though untested for the twin swap itself. The demo-day mitigation is to rehearse only the provided EV JSON and not let anyone change it to common kinds.

findings.title: k-anonymity is bypassable: exact totals, exact zeros and a product-owner-crafted moment reveal hidden cells and individual attributes
findings.detail: _k hides 1..9 but shows 0 exactly (engine.py:29), and the same response carries exact unsuppressed totals: signal_hits, beliefs, moments, customers_reached and messages_to_write (engine.py:237-241). (a) Default output: the suppressed cells are recoverable by subtraction. (b) Because a PO can create arbitrary moments (min_amount up to 1e7 and age/household/region predicates in dsl.py), a moment matching one customer can be probed: per-moment cells read '<10' or 0, and the exact totals change by exactly 1. README.md:132 claims 'counts under 10 are hidden'.
findings.evidence: exp6a.py. Default stats: states={'act':286,'advisor':45,'ask':2136,'deferred_fatigue':'<10','wait':18866}, beliefs=21334, so beliefs minus visible = 1 (actual deferred_fatigue rows = 1). per_moment moving_in_together.advisor='<10'; messages_to_write minus visible cells = 4 (actual = 4). Crafted moments (3 runs): notary min_amount = the single top payment EUR 56,774.57 (customer 30550, age 31): per_moment reach='<10', totals delta messages/moments/beliefs/signal_hits = +1. Adding age in [31,31]: still '<10' and +1. Age in [32,32]: per-moment reach=0 (exact zero) and deltas +0 (beliefs/signal_hits still +1). The attacker learns that the top notary-payer is 31, using only aggregates, from either the zero-vs-'<10' signal alone or the totals.
findings.fix: Suppress 0 as well ('<10' for 0..9) in _k; round or drop the exact totals in the PO payload (or apply complementary suppression); enforce a minimum cohort per custom moment (refuse to publish, or blur, any moment whose moments/reach is below K); restrict min_amount granularity (bucketed amounts). Rate limiting does not fix this.
findings.demo_impact: Not visible in the demo flow, but the README security section is the pitch for the Aikido business-logic audit, and this contradicts it with a 3-call reproduction. Expect it to be flagged if anyone probes PO aggregates.

reasons:
Reproduced on a scratchpad copy of the DB (100,000 customers), run against a copy of backend/mirror with no .env present. The mechanism is valid. The severity is overstated.

CONFIRMED
1. Subtraction recovers the suppressed cells. _k (engine.py:25-29) hides 1..9 but returns 0 exactly. The same response carries exact, unsuppressed totals (engine.py:233-241).
   - Default states were act 286, advisor 45, ask 2136, wait 18866 and deferred_fatigue '<10', with beliefs 21334. 21334 minus the visible states is 1, and a server-side count confirms deferred_fatigue = 1.
   - moving_in_together.advisor shows '<10'. states.advisor is exactly 45, so 45 - 16 - 13 - 12 = 4.
2. A PO-crafted moment singles out one customer (api.py:412-419, dsl.py:44 allows min_amount up to 1e7).
   - kind=notary, min_amount=56774.57 (customer 30550, age 31) gives deltas messages +1, moments +1, beliefs +1 and signal_hits +1. Per-moment reach reads '<10'.
   - To make age decisive, profile signals must act as additive evidence (dsl.py:201-205, only behavioural hits create a belief). I used notary weight 0.05, age weight 0.9 and ask threshold 0.5.
   - Age [31,31] and [31,40] give reach '<10' and +1 on messages and moments. Age [32,32] and [18,30] give reach exactly 0 and +0 on messages and moments, while beliefs and signal_hits stay +1.
   - So a PO can read that customer's age from aggregates alone, from the exact zero versus '<10', or from the exact totals.
3. The finding understates the impact. The care/vulnerability flag leaks the same way, because the advisor state is driven by c.vulnerable (dsl.py:227).
   - kind=other, min_amount=1714.35 (customer 53605, vulnerable=True) gives per_moment advisor='<10' and states.advisor +1.
   - kind=baby_store, min_amount=367.41 (customer 37884, vulnerable=False) gives advisor=0 and states.advisor +0.
4. Nothing blocks it. The only throttles are rate('write') 60/min and rate('run') 6/min (security.py:97-104) and MAX_CUSTOM_MOMENTS = 20 (engine.py:67). The tests (test_security.py:78-82, test_engine.py) only check that no names appear, with no small-cohort or differencing test. README.md:131 claims counts under 10 are hidden, which is true per cell but not for the response as a whole.

WHY NOT HIGH
- It needs an authenticated product_owner, an internal privileged role. The attacker must already hold the PO login, and the only write path is gated by role("product_owner") (api.py:412-413).
- No customer id or name is ever returned. The attacker learns a bare attribute (age, or the care flag) of an unnamed outlier customer. Tying it to a real person needs outside knowledge of that person's distinctive transaction.
- The data is synthetic and the flow is not visible in the 3-minute demo.
- The fix is cheap and local. Make _k suppress 0 as well, blur or round the exact totals, and refuse to publish custom moments whose cohort is below K.

It is still a real differencing flaw that contradicts the README privacy claim, so medium is fair for a real deployment. It is low priority for today's demo.

Scratch files are in the scratchpad under refute/ (probe.py, probe2.py, probe4.py). The live DB was locked by a running server, so I used an existing scratchpad copy (algviz/copy.duckdb). The project was not modified.

REPRODUCED. The finding is technically valid, but "high" is too strong and the demo impact is about nil, so I rate it medium.

How I ran it: the live mirror.duckdb and .wal were exclusively locked by the running server (open failed even with FileShare.ReadWrite). I used an existing scratchpad copy of the generated base DB (32,256,000 bytes, same size as live) and ran the real FastAPI app via TestClient against it, with a signed token for the seeded product_owner user. The script is scratchpad/refute_k/k_repro.py. Live numbers may differ slightly because of the WAL (feedback, runs), but the mechanism is identical.

Code confirmed:
- engine.py:29: `_k` returns n if n == 0 or n >= K_ANON, else "<10". Zero is shown exactly.
- engine.py:237-241: signal_hits, beliefs, moments, customers_reached and messages_to_write are returned as exact ints.
- No minimum cohort on custom moments. K_ANON is used only at engine.py:29 and 222-225 and api.py:444. `add_custom` (engine.py:63-73) only caps the count at 20.
- dsl.py:44 allows min_amount up to 1e7, and dsl.py:47-49 allows age, household_size and region predicates. A product owner can therefore craft a one-person moment via POST /api/po/moments.
- README.md claims "counts under 10 are hidden" at line 131, not 132 as the finding says. Trivial.

Output of k_repro.py:
(a) Default GET /api/po/funnel. states = {act 286, advisor 45, ask 2136, deferred_fatigue '<10', wait 18866}, beliefs = 21334. beliefs minus the visible states gives 1, and the DB truth is 1 deferred_fatigue row. messages_to_write is 2467 and the visible act+ask+advisor cells sum to 2463, a difference of 4. The DB truth for moving_in_together advisor is 4. Eleven zero cells are shown exactly.
(b) Crafted moments via POST /api/po/moments, then POST /api/po/run, then DELETE. The top notary payment is EUR 56,774.57 (customer 30550, age 31).
  - min_amount equal to that payment: reach '<10', totals delta messages/moments/beliefs/signal_hits all +1.
  - Same plus age in [31,31]: reach '<10', deltas +1.
  - Same plus age in [32,32]: reach is exact 0, messages and moments +0, beliefs and signal_hits still +1.
  So an attacker learns the top notary payer is 31, from either the '<10'-vs-0 signal or the exact totals.
(c) The exact totals alone leak even if `_k` were fixed. signal_hits delta equals the true number of customers with a notary payment >= X: 1 at 56,774.57, 1 at 56,773.57, 2 at 50,995.29. So the payment distribution can be binary-searched to the cent.

Why I downgrade it:
- It needs an authenticated product_owner, a privileged internal role. It needs an active multi-call differencing attack: create a moment, run, read, delete, repeat. The run limit of 6/min (security.py "run") only slows it; it is not a defence.
- The data is synthetic, and customers, advisors and unauthenticated users cannot reach it. It is a privacy-design gap, not an IDOR, authz bypass or injection.
- Within its own stated threat model, though, the k-anonymity claim is fully defeated with 3 calls. That is why it is not low.
- The default-output case (a) only recovers a count of 1 to 9 that carries no attributes. That is complementary suppression, a minor weakness. The real issue is (b) and (c).

Demo impact: none in the demo flow. Nothing in a normal 3-minute demo builds a narrow moment, and the built-in and example moments are broad. The only exposure is a judge or an automated Aikido-style scan actively probing PO aggregates. IDOR and authz scanners are unlikely to find this differencing attack. The real risk is rhetorical: the README "Security design" bullet at line 131 over-claims. Cheapest mitigation with no code change: reword it to "per-cell counts under 10 are hidden (no protection against differencing by a malicious product owner)". A code fix would be to refuse or blur custom moments below K and round the totals, but that is optional before today's demo.

findings.title: A DSL-valid moment with a huge integer value is persisted, then breaks every run AND every customer feedback/consent call, leaving a customer half-refreshed
findings.detail: Signal.value accepts any int (Scalar = Union[int,float,str], dsl.py:32,49), with only a type check (dsl.py:65-71) and no magnitude bound. A JSON integer of 39+ digits is accepted (HTTP 201) and persisted by add_custom (engine.py:69-73) without ever being executed. Binding it fails with 'Python integer too large for 128-bit integer type'. run_population then fails (500). refresh_customer fails for every customer, so the 'Not true' button (api.py:234) and the consent toggle (api.py:252) return 500 for everyone until a PO deletes the moment. There is no transaction: refresh_customer runs 'DELETE FROM signal_hits WHERE customer_id' (engine.py:113) before the failing INSERT (engine.py:114), so the customer's evidence is destroyed while their twin rows stay. my_feedback has already written the feedback row (api.py:229-233) when it fails.
findings.evidence: exp5.py/exp7.py. age >= 10**40, between [1,10**40] and in [10**40] are all ACCEPTED by the DSL and FAIL at execution. After add_custom: run_population raises InvalidInputException; refresh_customer(1) raises; delete_custom('poison') works and refresh then succeeds. Partial state for customer 1: before: twin rows 2, signal_hits rows 5; after failed refresh: twin rows 2, signal_hits rows 0; beliefs(1) then shows both ask states with 0 evidence items. (Float 1e40 is fine; other oddities like negative age, bool values, int 2**63, mixed int/float lists execute fine.)
findings.fix: Bound numeric values in Signal._check (e.g. age 0..130, household_size 0..50, abs(value) <= 1e9). In add_custom, compile and execute the moment once (dry-run against customers LIMIT 1) before INSERT and reject with 422/409 on any DB error. Wrap refresh_customer and run_population in BEGIN/COMMIT with rollback so a failure cannot leave hits deleted.
findings.demo_impact: Low probability (needs a 39-digit integer), but the failure mode is app-wide 500s on the core 'Not true' interaction until the moment is deleted.

reasons:
The defect is real and reproduces exactly as described, but the shipped UI cannot trigger it, so I rate it low rather than medium.

**Reproduced (scratch copies only, nothing in the project root touched):**
- Engine level, on a copy of a generated DB: `Signal.value` is `Union[int,float,str]` with only a type check (dsl.py:32,49,65-71), so `age >= 10**40`, `between [1,10**40]` and `in [10**40]` all pass `Moment.model_validate` and `model_validate_json`.
- `add_custom` (engine.py:63-73) inserts the moment without ever executing it.
- After that, `run_population` (engine.py:98) and `refresh_customer` (engine.py:114) raise `InvalidInputException: Python integer too large for 128-bit integer type`.
- The threshold is 10**39 and above. 10**38 and 2**63 still work. 2**127 fails with a different `ConversionException`.
- Partial state for customer 1 after the failed refresh: twin rows stay at 2, but `signal_hits` rows drop from 5 to 0. This is because `DELETE FROM signal_hits` (engine.py:113) runs before the failing INSERT, with no transaction.
- `delete_custom('poison')` restores a working refresh (hits back to 5).
- HTTP level, using TestClient on a freshly generated 4000-customer DB, logged in as `po` and `sofie`:
  - `POST /api/po/moments` with the 40-digit integer returns 201.
  - `POST /api/me/beliefs/buying_home/feedback` returns 500 (api.py:234), `PUT /api/me/consents` returns 500 (api.py:252), and `POST /api/po/run` returns 500.
  - The feedback row for Sofie was already persisted as `rejected` (api.py:229-233), yet her twin still shows `feedback=None`, and both beliefs show 0 evidence items.
  - `GET /api/me/twin`, `/api/me/guidance`, `/api/po/funnel` and `/api/po/moments` still return 200, and the DB connection stays usable afterwards.
  - `DELETE /api/po/moments/poison` returns 200, and feedback works again.
- I only ran customer 1 (Sofie). That every customer is affected follows from `compile_hits` binding every moment's parameters on every refresh (dsl.py:147-177, engine.py:109).

**Why it is weaker than stated (mitigating context):**
- **The shipped UI cannot produce the trigger.** The product-owner editor does `JSON.parse(editor)` and then `JSON.stringify` (web/src/views/ProductOwner.tsx:45,51 and web/src/api.ts:31), so a 40-digit integer becomes the float `1e+40`. In node, a 41-digit literal gives `{"value":1e+40}` and a 22-digit literal gives `1e+21`. The 21-digit case stays an integer, which DuckDB accepts.
- With `1e+40` in the body, the same HTTP flow returned 201 and then 200 for feedback, consent and run.
- Only a raw client such as curl, sending an authenticated `product_owner` request with a literal of 39+ digits, triggers it.
- It is reversible by deleting the moment, and the server survives a restart because `Engine.__init__` only re-runs the population when the tables are missing (engine.py:38-39).
- None of the four built-in YAML moments carries such a value.

**Conclusion:** an input-validation and atomicity gap with a clean repro, but the chance of hitting it in the 3-minute demo is about zero. The missing transaction around delete and insert in `refresh_customer` is the more general robustness point. The finding's fix (bounding numeric values, dry-running the moment before insert) is sound.

Scratch scripts: `refute_dsl/exp.py`, `httprepro.py` and `httprepro_ui.py` under the scratchpad.

The bug reproduces exactly as described, but the stated 'medium' and the demo impact are overstated, because the web app cannot send the triggering payload. I couldn't copy the live DB (it is locked), so I used a scratch copy of an earlier replica, db/replica.duckdb(+wal), in scratchpad/bigint_repro. Scripts: repro1.py (engine), repro_http.py (HTTP), repro2.py (DuckDB boundary).

REPRODUCED (engine). Signal.value is Union[int,float,str] with only a type check (dsl.py:49, 65-71), so ints of 10**39 and 10**40 and 2**127 and 2**128 all validate. add_custom (engine.py:63-73) inserts the moment without ever executing it. After that:
- run_population fails at engine.py:98 with "Python integer too large for 128-bit integer type". The failing CREATE OR REPLACE is atomic, so twin and signal_hits stay intact (25500 and 92550 rows).
- refresh_customer fails at engine.py:114 after the DELETE at engine.py:113 has already run. For customer 76282, twin rows stayed at 3 and signal_hits went from 8 to 0.
- beliefs() then returns the moments with 0 evidence items.
- delete_custom('poison') followed by refresh restored 8 hits.

REPRODUCED (HTTP, FastAPI TestClient with minted tokens, raw JSON body with a 41-digit integer, customer 1):
- POST /api/po/moments returns 201.
- POST /api/po/run returns 500 "Internal error".
- POST /api/me/beliefs/buying_home/feedback returns 500. The feedback row was already written by api.py:229-233: 'rejected' was persisted while the twin still showed 'act'.
- PUT /api/me/consents returns 500 (api.py:247-253).
- Customer 1's signal_hits fell from 5 to 0 while twin stayed at 3. GET /api/me/twin then returned buying_home 'act' with 0 evidence, which is a visibly wrong screen.
- DELETE /api/po/moments/poison returned 200, and the next PUT consents returned 200 with hits back at 5.
- Exact failure boundary: integers at or above 2**127 (39 digits), or at or below -(2**127)-1. 10**38 and 2**63/2**64 execute fine. Lists like [1, 10**40] for between, and [10**40] for in, also fail. A float 1e40 executes fine.

WHY IT IS LOW, NOT MEDIUM:
1. The web UI cannot produce the trigger. ProductOwner.tsx:45 does JSON.parse(editor) and api.ts:40 does JSON.stringify(opts.body). A 41-digit literal becomes the JS number 1e+40 and is sent as "1e+40", a float. In node, 1e40 became "1e+40", and integers of 21 digits or more also become exponent floats. Integers up to 20 digits stay integer literals, and those execute fine.
2. I sent exactly "1e+40" over HTTP on a fresh copy, which is what the UI would send. POST /api/po/run, feedback, consents and the twin read all returned 200, and nothing broke.
3. Only a hand-written 39-digit integer sent straight to the API can trigger it. That means curl, a script, or possibly Swagger at /api/docs, which is enabled in dev (api.py:60), and only with product_owner credentials. The demo's add-a-moment flow uses the fixed example in examples/ev_purchase.json / evExample.ts, which is unaffected.
4. The missing transaction around refresh_customer (engine.py:113-116) is real, but I found no other realistic trigger for a mid-refresh DB error in the code I read.

Outcome: valid robustness and hardening bug, near-zero chance of hitting it in the live 3-minute demo via the UI. A quick fix would be to bound values in Signal._check and to dry-run the compiled moment in add_custom before the INSERT. Wrapping the refresh in a transaction would also help.

findings.title: Performance claim in README and demo script ('under a second', 0.6 to 1 s) not reproduced: 2.5 to 3.7 s baseline, 4 to 6 s with the EV moment; 'evidence' column is dead weight
findings.detail: README.md:17, :102 and :119 say new moments go live 'in under a second' and a full run takes 0.6 to 1 s. The PO screen prints the real run_ms (ProductOwner.tsx:87), so the audience will see a number that contradicts the script. The twin stage dominates, not the 6M-event scan. Part of the cost is dead: twin.evidence (list(signal_id ORDER BY weight DESC), dsl.py:202 and :214) is never read; beliefs() gets evidence from signal_hits (engine.py:125-127) and api.py only uses b['evidence'] built from there.
findings.evidence: exp1/exp5/exp7/exp8 on 100k. run_ms: 2498 (first), 2762/3188/3041 (repeat), 3762 after adding EV. Breakdown (builtin): hits 0.55 to 2.93 s, twin 2.26 to 2.78 s, stats 0.09 to 0.13 s. Builtin+EV: hits 0.87 s, twin 4.87 s. exp8: the aggregation step costs 513 ms with list(... ORDER BY) and 178 ms without; full twin_sql 1517 ms with default 16 threads vs 670 ms with threads=1 (noisy, shared host). Numbers may be better on a quiet machine.
findings.fix: Drop the evidence column and list() from twin_sql (saves roughly a third of the aggregation time here); try SET threads to 4 to 8 for these small tables; measure on the actual demo laptop, then change the script and README to the measured number ('a few seconds') or say 'about N s'.
findings.demo_impact: The presenter says 'under a second' while the screen shows 2,500 to 4,000 ms; a judge can catch it. Cheap to fix by wording.

reasons:
Reproduced, with one correction: the proposed fix saves far more than "roughly a third".

**Claim in text.** README.md:17 says "live for everyone in under a second", :102 says "under a second" and :119 says "0.6 to 1 s". ProductOwner.tsx:87 and :102 print the measured `run_ms` to the audience. `run_ms` covers `sync_runtime`, the `signal_hits` CTAS and the `twin` CTAS, at engine.py:91-100.

**Setup.** The live mirror.duckdb and .wal are locked by a running server, so I could not copy them. I used an equivalent seed-42 copy from earlier in this scratchpad (corr/base.duckdb: 100,000 customers, 6,116,388 events) in scratchpad/rfut_perf, running the project's own Engine, dsl and DuckDB 1.5.6 (Python 3.14.5, 16 threads).

**Load caveat.** The host was at 91-94% CPU from other agents, so absolute numbers are pessimistic. Even so, nothing came close to 0.6-1 s.

**Run times.**
- `run_population()` with the 4 built-in moments: [6409 (cold), 3402, 2886, 2877, 2474] ms.
- After adding ev_purchase: [3097, 4347, 4742, 3763, 3822] ms.
- Recorded run_ms in the `runs` tables of other fresh generated copies: 1751, 2441, 2731, 2751, 2925 ms. None is under 1 s.

**Breakdown (built-in moments / with EV).**
- hits: 659-1052 ms / 814-1405 ms.
- twin: 1942-2332 ms / 2690-2832 ms.
- stats: about 130-200 ms.
- The twin stage dominates, as the reviewer said.

**evidence is dead weight.**
- `twin.evidence` (dsl.py:202, :214, :239) is never read.
- engine.py:121-122 selects explicit columns without it, and the stats queries at engine.py:177-196 don't touch it.
- The API's `b["evidence"]` at api.py:278 and :384 comes from `signal_hits` via engine.py:125-127 and :141-152.
- Nothing in tests or web/ reads it from the `twin` table.

**Fix effect (bench2.py).** Replacing `list(signal_id ORDER BY weight DESC)` with an empty list gives 0 differing rows versus the original `twin` (25,499 rows each), apart from the evidence column. At 16 threads, `twin` drops from 1952 ms min / 2338 ms median to 216 ms min / 306 ms median. That is roughly a 90% cut in the twin stage, not "a third". Thread count barely matters once evidence is gone.

**Still not sub-second.** After the fix, hits (0.6-1.4 s here) plus twin (0.2-0.3 s) is about 0.8-1.7 s. A no-evidence full run measured 1261-1862 ms, so "under a second" stays borderline on this host. The wording should still change to the measured figure.

**Not refuted.** Nothing in the code, tests or UI guards or softens the claim. The "in our test environment" hedge in README.md:119 is the only mitigation, and it does not cover the spoken "under a second" at :102.

**Severity.** Medium: it is a visible on-screen contradiction in a live demo, and the wording fix is cheap.

Reproduced. The claim is stated at README.md:17 ("live for everyone in under a second"), :102 ("under a second") and :119 ("0.6 to 1 s"). The PO screen prints the real value at web/src/views/ProductOwner.tsx:87 and :102. "Validate & go live" runs the moment add and then run() at ProductOwner.tsx:51-54, so the EV moment shows the same run_ms. run_ms is taken at engine.py:100, after signal_hits and twin but before stats(), so it is hits + twin only.

I could not copy the live DB (exclusively locked), so I generated my own population with `python -m mirror.generate --customers 100000 --seed 42` into the scratchpad (6,116,388 events) and ran `Engine.run_population()` on it. The host was about 80% CPU-loaded by other agents, so absolute numbers are pessimistic. Scripts and DB are in scratchpad/refute_perf_claim (bench.py, bench2.py, bench3.py). Nothing in the project root was touched.

- **Built-in moments (4):** run_ms was 1727, 1910, 2650, 3021, 3027 (median 2650). The best case I ever saw was 1.7 s; it was never under 1 s. Interleaved A/B runs gave totals of 2.7 to 3.9 s.
- **With the EV moment (5):** run_ms was 2963, 3126, 3240, 2843, 3320 (median 3126).
- **Breakdown:** the twin step dominates (about 1.8 to 2.6 s, min 1784 ms). The hits scan is 0.65 to 2.5 s and stats() is 0.07 to 0.18 s. The reviewer's figures (2.5 to 3.7 s) are reproduced.
- **Dead column:** `list(signal_id ORDER BY weight DESC) AS evidence` (dsl.py:202, :214, :239) is never read. engine.py:120-130 selects explicit columns from twin, and beliefs() builds its evidence from signal_hits (engine.py:125-127, :141-152).

Two corrections to the reviewer's detail:
- **The fix is much stronger than "roughly a third".** With the evidence column removed, the twin step falls from a 2.4 s median (min 1992) to 0.17 to 0.27 s. Total hits + twin falls from 3.4 to 3.6 s to 1.1 to 1.3 s (min 899 ms). Output is identical: a symmetric EXCEPT over customer_id, moment_id, confidence, inferred, feedback, priority, ask_t, act_t, state returned 0 rows, with 25,499 rows on each side. With the list column, `SET threads` moves the twin time around (threads=1: 1.1 s median vs 2.4 s at 16), but once the list is gone threads no longer matter, so thread tuning is unnecessary.
- **"Under a second" is still borderline after the fix.** I measured 0.9 to 1.3 s on a loaded host. It is plausible on a quiet machine, but it must be re-measured on the demo laptop before keeping the wording.

I kept the severity at medium. It is a wording contradiction, not a functional bug, and the fix is a few lines or a sentence. But the number is shown twice on screen (hero sentence and "Run time" KPI, 2.5 to 3.8 s) at 0:20 and 2:15, right next to a script line saying "under a second". Given the README's own "read these honestly" framing, that is a credibility risk if a judge notices. The demo impact is as the reviewer stated.

Recommended fix: drop the evidence column and list() from twin_sql, re-measure on the demo machine, then write "about N s" in README.md:17, :102 and :119 and in the spoken script.

findings.title: Cached intro text survives consent withdrawal and still names the withdrawn data
findings.detail: message_cache is keyed on (customer, moment, state, lang, channel) and read before the evidence is used (channels.py:128-131). refresh_customer/consent changes never invalidate it, so if the state stays the same the old text, built from now-unconsented evidence, is reused. (The 'why' line is recomputed and is correct; the intro is not.) With the built-in moments and template mode this is not reachable through demo users (their state drops to 'wait'), but it is reachable with any custom moment whose remaining evidence stays above the ask threshold, and with LLM mode (facts include why=labels, channels.py:138) for a confirmed 'act' item (not executed: no key).
findings.evidence: exp10.py via TestClient on the scratch DB with a custom moment [notary tx 0.5 + mortgage_simulation app 0.4, ask 0.35]. Before: intro='Hi Sofie, based on a transfer to a notary and a mortgage simulation in the app, ...'. After PUT /api/me/consents transactions=false: twin evidence sources=['app'], state still 'ask', why='a mortgage simulation in the app', but intro is still 'based on a transfer to a notary and a mortgage simulation in the app ...'. delete_custom (engine.py:75-83) also never touches message_cache (by code; not executed).
findings.fix: Delete the customer's message_cache rows in refresh_customer (or key the cache on a hash of the evidence signal ids), and delete by moment_id in delete_custom.
findings.demo_impact: Not triggered by the scripted demo. It is a real violation of the 'consent enforced' claim if a judge withdraws consent on a customer with a custom moment active.

reasons:
Confirmed, and it is more reachable than the reviewer said. Code: channels.py:127-131 returns any message_cache hit keyed only on (customer, moment, state, lang, channel) before using the evidence labels. The only writer is the INSERT OR REPLACE at channels.py:145-149. A grep for message_cache across backend/*.py finds only channels.py and db.py:82, so nothing ever invalidates it. refresh_customer (engine.py:106-116) and my_consents (api.py:244-253) never touch the table, and delete_custom (engine.py:75-83) doesn't either. There is no TTL, and no test covers it (test_security.py:146-152 only checks the twin payload after withdrawing transactions).

I ran it on a scratch copy of the pristine DB. I used TestClient, Gemini and ElevenLabs keys blanked in config, and only the built-in moments in template mode.

1) Demo user sofie (customer 1), no custom moment. Before: buying_home is 'ask' at 0.82, intro "Hi Sofie, based on a transfer to a notary and a mortgage simulation in the app, ...". I then did PUT /api/me/consents {transactions:true, app:false}. The twin now gives buying_home 'ask' at 0.64, evidence only notary_deposit plus the profile signal, and the 'why' line is "a transfer to a notary". The intro, served from cache, still says "based on a transfer to a notary and a mortgage simulation in the app". The reviewer's claim that demo users drop to 'wait' only holds when transactions consent is withdrawn (0.55 < 0.6). Withdrawing the app consent leaves Sofie at 0.64, above the 0.6 ask threshold. The Mirror page has the consent toggles (web/src/views/Mirror.tsx around lines 92-107), and mutate() re-fetches /me/guidance (Mirror.tsx:18, 36). A judge flipping "app activity" off on Sofie would see the intro and the 'why' line contradict each other, against the README claim "Consent is enforced in the query: switched-off data is never read".

2) LLM mode, simulated. I monkeypatched channels._gemini to echo facts["why"]; no real LLM was called. With buying_home confirmed ('act', state unchanged by consent), the cached LLM-style intro kept the withdrawn "a mortgage simulation in the app" after the app consent was withdrawn. voice_script (channels.py:153) reads the same cached intro (api.py:306-312), so the voice note would speak it too.

3) delete_custom. I created custom moment cm_test, ran the population, and Sofie's guidance was cached. After DELETE /api/po/moments/cm_test the message_cache row is still there. Re-creating the same id with a new label and running again gives a 'why' of "NEW LABEL evidence", but the intro still says "based on OLD LABEL evidence". This matters if the product-owner step is rehearsed and repeated with the same id.

Lucas does not trigger it, because his state changes on consent withdrawal and so the cache key changes. The stated severity of medium is too low: the reviewer's premise that built-in moments and demo users can't reach it is wrong. It shows on the main demo customer's screen with default data and contradicts the headline consent claim. The fix is small: DELETE FROM message_cache WHERE customer_id=$cid inside the lock in refresh_customer, and DELETE ... WHERE moment_id=$id in delete_custom.

Files read: mirror/backend/mirror/channels.py, engine.py, api.py, db.py, dsl.py, config.py, generate.py, the moments YAML, backend/tests/test_security.py, and web/src/views/Mirror.tsx. The live DB was locked, so I used a copy of the pristine DB already in the scratchpad, and my scripts are in scratchpad/refute_cache. No project files were changed.

VALID, but the demo-impact claim is wrong. Code: message_cache is read at channels.py:128-131 keyed on (customer, moment, state, lang, channel). Nothing invalidates it. refresh_customer (engine.py:106-116) never touches it. delete_custom (engine.py:75-83) only deletes custom_moments, twin and signal_hits. A grep of backend/mirror finds message_cache only in channels.py and db.py:82.

Reproduction on a freshly generated scratch DB (the live DB is exclusively locked, so I generated one with the conftest settings; LLM and TTS keys blanked, so template mode). Scripts are rc2.py and rc3.py in scratchpad/refute_cache2.

1. The finding's custom-moment repro reproduces exactly. Sofie, custom moment [notary tx 0.5 + mortgage_simulation app 0.4, ask 0.35]:
   - Before: intro is 'based on a transfer to a notary and a mortgage simulation in the app'.
   - After PUT /api/me/consents transactions=false: state is still 'ask', why is correct ('a mortgage simulation in the app'), but the intro is unchanged and still names the notary transfer.

2. delete_custom orphans cache rows (now executed, not just by code). After DELETE /api/po/moments/cust_a the row (cust_a, ask) remains. Re-creating the same id with a new signal label then serves the OLD intro text while the why line shows the new label.

3. The claim that this is not reachable with built-in moments and demo users is FALSE. Sofie (the headline demo customer) with the built-in buying_home moment:
   - All consents on: 'ask', 0.82, intro 'Hi Sofie, based on a transfer to a notary and a mortgage simulation in the app, ...'.
   - Toggle app data off, which is one click on the Mirror page (web/src/views/Mirror.tsx:101-107, which calls PUT /me/consents and then reloads guidance).
   - Twin: state stays 'ask' (notary 0.6 + profile 0.1 = 0.64, still at or above ask 0.6). Evidence is ['a transfer to a notary', 'your life stage'], why is 'a transfer to a notary'.
   - The guidance intro is unchanged and still says 'and a mortgage simulation in the app'.
   - Only the transactions toggle drops Sofie to 'wait'.
   - Lucas (act to ask) and Marc (advisor) are not affected in template mode, because the state changes or the act/advisor templates carry no evidence text.

UI effect: the 'ask' card hides the why line (Mirror.tsx:249 shows it only when type !== 'ask'), so the stale intro is the only evidence text on that card. It visibly contradicts the belief card on the left, which no longer lists the app signal. The voice script (api.py:312) would speak the same stale intro. The underlying data is not read (the query-level consent filter still works), so this is a stale-text and trust bug, not a data-processing leak.

Severity: medium is right. It is cosmetic to the decision logic but contradicts the README claim at README.md:135 ('Consent is enforced... switched-off data is never read'). Demo impact is higher than stated: the scripted 3-minute demo does not toggle consent, but a judge clicking 'app data' off on Sofie would hit it with no custom moment needed. The fix is one line: DELETE FROM message_cache WHERE customer_id=$cid inside refresh_customer, and DELETE FROM message_cache WHERE moment_id=$id in delete_custom.

findings.title: 'At least one behavioural signal' guard is bypassed by a behavioural signal of weight 1e-300, which lets a profile-only moment target everyone
findings.detail: The validator only checks source != 'profile' (dsl.py:128-129) and twin_sql requires count(behav) > 0 (dsl.py:201,205), not any minimum weight, and weight only needs gt=0 (dsl.py:40). test_security.py:100-102 tests that a profile-only moment is rejected because it 'would target everyone of an age'; adding a near-zero-weight behavioural signal defeats that protection.
findings.evidence: exp11.py: moment = [login app weight 1e-300] + [age >= 18 weight 0.95]: act=82,047, advisor=1,702 of 100,000 customers, inferred=0.95 for all of them, ai_share_of_customers=0.862. The validator accepts weight=1e-300.
findings.fix: Raise the weight floor (e.g. ge=0.05) and/or require that the noisy-OR of a moment's profile signals alone stays below thresholds.ask, so demographics can never carry a decision.
findings.demo_impact: Only reachable by a PO. It allows mass-targeting by age with no behavioural evidence, contradicting the README guardrail story.

reasons:
The bypass reproduces, but it is a low-severity hardening gap, not a medium guardrail failure. I ran a probe on a scratchpad copy of the DB (100,000 customers) through Moment.model_validate_json, Engine.add_custom and run_population.

**What is true.** The validator at dsl.py:128-129 only checks `source != "profile"`. The weight field at dsl.py:40 is `gt=0, le=0.95`, and twin_sql at dsl.py:201/205 only needs `count(behav) > 0`. A moment of [app login, weight 1e-300] plus [age >= 18, weight 0.95] is accepted. It produced 83,760 twin rows: act 82,057, advisor 1,702, deferred_fatigue 1, with inferred 0.95 for all. A profile-only moment is rejected ("a moment needs at least one behavioural signal"), as test_security.py:100-102 expects. The reviewer's 82,047 act figure differs slightly from my 82,057, which is just copy-state noise.

**Why the severity and framing are wrong.**
- **The proposed fix does not work.** With weight 0.05, the floor the reviewer suggests, the outcome is identical (probe C: 82,057 act, 1,702 advisor, inferred 0.9525). The tiny weight is irrelevant. A weak-but-ubiquitous behavioural signal is enough, because login is held by about 84.7% of customers.
- **No new capability.** A single legitimate app-login signal at weight 0.95, with no profile signal at all, produces the same targeting (probe F: act 82,057, advisor 1,702). A PO can already reach this population through the normal DSL, so the "at least one behavioural signal" check was never a targeting guard. It is a sanity check, filed in test_security.py under "no injection / nonsense".
- **The real guardrails still hold.** Consent is enforced in compile_hits at dsl.py:137/163: 0 targeted customers lacked consent_app. min_age (dsl.py:226), the vulnerable-to-advisor rule (dsl.py:227, 1,702 customers routed to an advisor) and the max_active fatigue cap all still apply.
- **The README makes no contradicted claim.** README.md:20 and :135 promise consent, suitability and care guardrails, and all of those are intact. Nothing promises that demographics cannot carry a decision.
- **Scope is narrow.** The endpoint is POST /api/po/moments, which requires the product_owner role (api.py:413).

**Only fix that would help.** Bound the noisy-OR of a moment's profile signals below thresholds.ask. A weight floor alone would not.

**Demo impact.** None.

Reproduced, but the finding is overstated. The bypass is real, yet the guard is cosmetic and any PO can reach the same outcome with a fully legitimate definition, so it is not a security flaw and the demo impact is nil.

What reproduces (scratch script refute_dsl2/repro.py in the scratchpad, using dsl.py and duckdb only; .env never loaded):
- dsl.py:128-129 only checks `s.source != "profile"`. dsl.py:40 is `weight: float = Field(gt=0, le=0.95)`, so 1e-300 validates.
- A moment of [app login, weight 1e-300] + [age >= 18, weight 0.95] passes `Moment.model_validate`. On the DB copy, compile_hits plus twin_sql gives inferred = 0.95 for every hit. That is 76,071 act + 1,581 advisor = 77,652 customers, i.e. everyone with consent_app and a login in the last 90 days.
- My counts differ from the reporter's 82,047/1,702. I had to use an existing scratchpad replica of mirror.duckdb, because the live file and its .wal are exclusively locked by the running server and cannot be copied.
- The same moment without the behavioural signal is rejected at dsl.py:129. The test at test_security.py:100-102 still passes.

Why the severity and demo impact are wrong:
1. The 1e-300 trick is not needed. A single login signal with weight 0.95 and no profile signal, using the default thresholds 0.6/0.8, yields the identical 76,071 act + 1,581 advisor. So does login weight 0.06 with thresholds ask 0.05 / act 0.06 (the allowed minimum). The "at least one behavioural signal" rule never limited how many people a PO-authored moment reaches, because the PO sets weights and thresholds.
2. The proposed fix `weight ge=0.05` does not help. Login weight 0.05 plus age 0.95 gives inferred 0.9525 for the same 77,652 customers.
3. The second suggested fix, keeping a moment's profile signals alone below thresholds.ask, would close the demographic-only route. But a PO could still make login alone carry the decision, so it does not stop mass targeting.
4. Only the product_owner role reaches this. POST /api/po/moments is gated by `role("product_owner")` (api.py:413) and rate-limited (api.py:414).
5. The real guardrails still hold on such a moment, because they sit in the engine:
   - Consent is applied inside compile_hits (dsl.py:163), so the 15,235 customers without app consent are excluded.
   - min_age and the vulnerable-customer rule apply in twin_sql, so 1,581 of the hits land in 'advisor' rather than 'act'.
   - Fatigue caps each customer at MAX_ACTIVE=2.
   - Custom moments are capped at 20 and can be deleted.
6. The README makes no claim about profile-only moments. The only stated intent is the comment at test_security.py:102.
7. The demo flow uses backend/examples/ev_purchase.json, which is unaffected.

The most realistic impact is a PO-crafted priority-100 moment crowding out built-in moments of priority 60-90 in the 2-slot fatigue ranking. That needs a deliberately hostile PO and is reversible by delete.

Verdict: a valid observation about a weak validator, but low severity, a policy gap rather than a vulnerability, with no effect on the 3-minute demo.

low_unverified.title: delete_custom leaves stale fatigue states; feedback (and cached messages) persist and re-apply to a re-created moment id
low_unverified.detail: delete_custom deletes the moment's twin and hits rows but does not re-rank the customers it affected, so rows that were 'deferred_fatigue' because of it stay deferred until the next full run. It also never deletes feedback rows, so a customer's confirm/reject for a deleted id re-applies to any later moment created with that id, even with a completely different definition. The UI always runs a full population right after delete (ProductOwner.tsx:62-63), which fixes the fatigue staleness, so this matters for direct API use and for rehearsal with re-created ev_purchase. Related: the cap only applies to act/ask, so 'advisor' rows are uncapped, and a third customer-confirmed moment silently becomes 'deferred_fatigue'. In natural data only 1 of 100,000 customers hits the cap.
low_unverified.evidence: exp4.py. Customer 91741 had growing_family=act, hi_prio=ask, buying_home=deferred_fatigue; after delete_custom('hi_prio') the stored twin still says buying_home=deferred_fatigue, while refresh_customer gives 'ask'; deferred_fatigue rows 36 before vs 2 after the next full run. Customer 4 rejected ev_purchase, the moment was deleted and re-created with a different definition: twin row = suppressed_feedback, confidence 0.0, inferred 0.9. Feedback rows remaining after delete: 1. Vulnerable customers with three extra custom moments: 4 'advisor' rows, 0 act/ask. message_cache non-purge is by code reading (not executed).
low_unverified.fix: In delete_custom also DELETE FROM feedback and message_cache WHERE moment_id=$id, and refresh the affected customers (or trigger run_population). Decide whether advisor rows should count toward the cap, and surface 'deferred' to a customer who just confirmed.
low_unverified.demo_impact: Minor. Would show only if the PO deletes and re-adds the same EV id during rehearsal after customers interacted with it.

low_unverified.title: Noisy-OR exp(sum(ln(1-w))) is not exact at thresholds: 16 of 91 two-decimal weights land below themselves
low_unverified.detail: confidence >= ask_t / act_t (dsl.py:225,229) uses raw doubles. For custom moments where a noisy-OR is mathematically equal to a threshold, rounding error of about 1e-16 flips the decision to a lower state. No built-in or the EV example is affected: the only exact-threshold combination across built-ins+EV is notary_deposit alone (0.6 vs ask 0.6), and it evaluates to exactly 0.6 and passes.
low_unverified.evidence: exp2.py/exp2b.py/exp12.py: single-signal moments with weight == ask threshold fail for w in {0.08,0.09,0.10,0.11,0.18,0.19,0.20,0.21,0.22,0.23,0.41,...,0.46} (16/91); 21 of 157 two-signal combos that are exactly on a 2-decimal threshold fail, e.g. 1-(0.9*0.9)=0.19 evaluates to 0.18999999999999995. Replacing ln/exp with DuckDB's product() does NOT fix it (still 16/16 and 21/21 failures), because 1-(1-w) is itself inexact.
low_unverified.fix: Compare with a tolerance: confidence >= ask_t - 1e-9 and confidence >= act_t - 1e-9 (the errors are about 1e-16); or compute in DECIMAL. The epsilon fix was not executed, only reasoned from the observed error size.
low_unverified.demo_impact: Only if someone sets a custom threshold equal to an achievable confidence, e.g. ask=0.45 with a single 0.45 signal, in which case 'exactly at threshold' customers silently wait.

low_unverified.title: tests/test_engine.py: fatigue-cap test is vacuous and the refresh-vs-population test covers one customer with no feedback
low_unverified.detail: test_fatigue_cap (lines 14-19) asserts max act/ask per customer <= MAX_ACTIVE, but the conftest population (4000, seed 7) never produces a customer with more than 2 candidates, so the assertion passes even with the cap removed. test_single_customer_refresh_matches_population (lines 22-27) checks only customer 1 (Sofie), rounds confidence to 6 decimals, and has no feedback or consent change. The underlying properties do hold (see summary), but the tests would not catch a regression. In the 100k data the cap is exercised by 1 customer.
low_unverified.evidence: exp6c.py: generate(4000, seed=7): with cap=2 max act/ask per customer = 2 and deferred_fatigue rows = 0; with MAX_ACTIVE lifted to 99 max act/ask per customer is still 2, so the test cannot fail. exp6a.py E: natural 100k with cap lifted has exactly 1 customer with more than 2 candidates (max 3). 22 tests pass per the existing scratchpad/pytest1.txt run.
low_unverified.fix: Seed a customer with 3 confirmed or strong moments (insert feedback confirmed on 3 moments) and assert exactly 2 stay active and the third is deferred_fatigue. Extend the refresh test to a sample of customers, both with and without feedback and with a consent change, and compare full rows including state and feedback (my exp3.py does this).
low_unverified.demo_impact: None on stage; it is a test-quality gap that matters if the code is reviewed or changed under time pressure.

low_unverified.title: conftest disables AI keys, then config.py reloads them from .env; tests can hit live Gemini/ElevenLabs or become flaky
low_unverified.detail: conftest.py:12-14 pops GEMINI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT/ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, but conftest.py:18-19 then imports mirror.generate, which imports mirror.config, whose _load_dotenv() (config.py:30) sets any key that is 'not in os.environ' (config.py:26), so a developer's .env re-populates the keys the test tried to remove. I could not check the real .env (not read, per instructions). If it contains these keys, test_guidance_falls_back_to_templates_without_ai (test_engine.py:30-33) and test_voice_only_for_own_active_guidance (test_security.py:176, expects 503 'not configured') depend on the network and on the keys being invalid. The existing 22-pass run in the scratchpad is consistent with either case.
low_unverified.evidence: Reproduced in a fake tree (scratchpad/corr/fakeproj): config.py copy + a .env containing GEMINI_API_KEY=fake and ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=fake; after os.environ.pop(...) as in conftest and 'from mirror import config': config.GEMINI_API_KEY set = True, ELEVENLABS set = True.
low_unverified.fix: In conftest, set the keys to empty strings instead of popping them (an empty-but-present env var blocks the .env loader because of the 'key not in os.environ' check), or add a MIRROR_DISABLE_DOTENV switch honoured by config.
low_unverified.demo_impact: None on stage. It affects whether tests are hermetic when run on the demo machine, and it can spend API quota.

low_unverified.title: run_population compiles from a moment snapshot taken outside the lock (TOCTOU), plus other unlocked check-then-act windows
low_unverified.detail: run_population reads moments and compiles the SQL at engine.py:93-95 before taking db.lock at :96, then sync_runtime() inside the lock re-reads the moments. A concurrent add_custom/delete_custom landing in between yields moments_rt that disagrees with signal_hits/twin. api.py:221 checks that a moment exists outside the lock that protects the feedback write (:224). beliefs() reads twin and signal_hits in separate lock acquisitions (engine.py:120-130), so a concurrent run can mix generations. In practice the window is milliseconds and the UI sequences add then run; I forced it by monkeypatching, not by timing.
low_unverified.evidence: exp9.py: hooking compile_hits to call add_custom(ev) before it returns (an add arriving inside the window) gave moments_rt has EV=1, signal_hits rows for EV=0, twin rows for EV=0, and the run's stats row for ev_purchase = act 0, ask 0, reach 0, recall 0.0 (reports live but reaching nobody until the next Run). The delete variant would leave orphan signal_hits (by code; not run).
low_unverified.fix: Move the moments snapshot and compile_hits inside the with self.db.lock block (cheap), and re-check moment existence inside the lock in my_feedback.

low_unverified.title: Product-owner stats semantics: funnel goes stale after customer actions; 'ai_share_of_customers' counts messages, not customers
low_unverified.detail: last_stats() (engine.py:256-258) returns the last run's JSON, and /api/po/funnel (api.py:437-438) serves it; refresh_customer never updates it, so customer feedback, such as Sofie's 'Not true', does not change rejected_by_customer or any count until the PO presses Run (by code reading; not executed via the API). ai_share_of_customers = messages / customers (engine.py:241-242), where messages counts act+ask+advisor rows, so a customer with two items is counted twice, while README.md:119 says '2.5% of customers get a message'.
low_unverified.evidence: Code: engine.py:106-116 (refresh has no stats update) vs :256-258. Numbers: messages 2,467 vs distinct act/ask customers 2,397 (plus advisor customers) on 100,000; after EV 2,910 messages vs 2,819 distinct reached.
low_unverified.fix: Either recompute the cheap aggregates (states, per-moment state counts) on read, or label the funnel 'as of last run'. Compute the share from count(DISTINCT customer_id) over active states.
low_unverified.demo_impact: In the script order (PO run, then Sofie, then PO adds EV and runs) the numbers are fresh when shown; only a PO funnel reload between customer actions would look stale.

low_unverified.title: within_days uses a strict '>' so 'within N days' actually covers N-1 days
low_unverified.detail: The compiled predicate is e.ts > CAST($now AS DATE) - CAST(N AS INTEGER), so events exactly N days old are excluded. The generator plants days_ago in [0,180) (config.SIM_DAYS), so the off-by-one is visible but tiny in the recall numbers.
low_unverified.evidence: exp9.py: notary events with amount >= 1000 that are exactly 119 days old: 13 (included); exactly 120 days old: 12 (excluded by 'within_days: 120'); 121 days: 5; for exactly-120-day-old events the compiled predicate matches 0.
low_unverified.fix: Use >= now - N (or document the semantics as 'the last N-1 days plus today').

low_unverified.title: The 'existing EV owners' confounder cannot fire at the shipped thresholds
low_unverified.detail: generate.py:213-215 plants 3% EV owners emitting 4 to 15 ev_charging events as a deliberate confounder (README.md:92 area describes confounders as a design feature). In examples/ev_purchase.json charging alone has weight 0.4 and car insurance 0.3; 1-(0.6*0.7)=0.58 is below ask 0.6, so owners can never reach 'ask' without a dealer payment, and EV precision is structurally about 100%. The gift-buyer (toy/baby) confounder, by contrast, does bite (growing_family precision 46%).
low_unverified.evidence: Weights: 0.4 and 0.4+0.3 give 0.4 and 0.58 versus ask 0.6, all below ask. Observed EV precision 0.998 (434 detected, about 1 false positive) and precision_act 1.0 on the scratch run.
low_unverified.fix: Either lower the EV ask threshold in the example so the confounder produces visible false positives, or describe the EV-owner confounder as a 'negative control' (the engine correctly ignores it) in the demo talk track.
low_unverified.demo_impact: Only narrative: don't claim the engine 'beat' the EV-owner confounder as evidence of accuracy, since it cannot fail there.
